cards.headline: Vero Beach man held on $1 million bond for creating AI deepfake sexual images
cards.teaser: A Vero Beach man was arrested Wednesday and is being held on a $1 million bond after creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent. Peter
cards.body:
A Vero Beach man was arrested Wednesday and is being held on a $1 million bond after creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent. Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, faces eight charges stemming from incidents occurring between June and August 2026 relating to one female victim. The charges include three counts of creating altered sexual depictions, three counts of promoting those depictions, one count of sexual cyber harassment, and one count of stalking.

 Officers with the Vero Beach Police Department say Ruma took photos from social media and other online sources to create some of the altered images. Investigators searched Ruma's home and electronic devices on Wednesday and found evidence connecting back to the creation and distribution of the AI-generated images. An arrest warrant was obtained after the investigation.

 Police have identified several additional potential victims who have not been identified or may not know images of them were created or shared. Investigators also believe Ruma may have engaged in this conduct for years. Court records show Ruma has a prior criminal history in Indian River County.

 In 2007, he was arrested on charges that included burglary and sex battery on a physically impaired person. In 2009, he was arrested on a burglary charge and was later sentenced to the Florida Department of Corrections.

 Investigators are publicly urging anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has received, viewed, or has information regarding the altered or explicit images, to contact the Vero Beach Police Department. The investigation is still ongoing, and additional charges could be filed. Federal officials recently launched TakeItDown.FTC.gov, a resource that allows victims to report nonconsensual intimate images and seek their removal from online platforms.

hero.headline: Vero Beach man held on $1 million bond for creating AI deepfake sexual images
hero.teaser: A Vero Beach man was arrested Wednesday and is being held on a $1 million bond after creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent. Peter
hero.body:
A Vero Beach man was arrested Wednesday and is being held on a $1 million bond after creating and distributing AI-generated sexually explicit images of women without consent. Peter Solomon Ruma, 37, faces eight charges stemming from incidents occurring between June and August 2026 relating to one female victim. The charges include three counts of creating altered sexual depictions, three counts of promoting those depictions, one count of sexual cyber harassment, and one count of stalking.

 Officers with the Vero Beach Police Department say Ruma took photos from social media and other online sources to create some of the altered images. Investigators searched Ruma's home and electronic devices on Wednesday and found evidence connecting back to the creation and distribution of the AI-generated images. An arrest warrant was obtained after the investigation.

 Police have identified several additional potential victims who have not been identified or may not know images of them were created or shared. Investigators also believe Ruma may have engaged in this conduct for years. Court records show Ruma has a prior criminal history in Indian River County.

 In 2007, he was arrested on charges that included burglary and sex battery on a physically impaired person. In 2009, he was arrested on a burglary charge and was later sentenced to the Florida Department of Corrections.

 Investigators are publicly urging anyone who believes they may have been victimized, or who has received, viewed, or has information regarding the altered or explicit images, to contact the Vero Beach Police Department. The investigation is still ongoing, and additional charges could be filed. Federal officials recently launched TakeItDown.FTC.gov, a resource that allows victims to report nonconsensual intimate images and seek their removal from online platforms.
